_comment: The coach-mark tutorial. Sean, 23 September: *"The tutorial stays on one screen. It needs to walk you through various screens ideally asking you to click on things. Imagine it like someone showing you a tour of the UI."* So every step but the last points at a real element on the live game, most of them ask you to tap it, and tapping it is what moves the tour on. Next is always there for somebody who would rather just read.
_targets: `target` is a `data-tour` attribute the UI carries: map, island, island-tabs, build, book, log, clock, purse, advisor, info. **A step whose target is not on screen is skipped silently** — that is what lets the tour walk through sheets without knowing whether the player followed it, and what stops a rearranged screen breaking the tour instead of degrading it.
_rules: Keep every body under about forty words and name the thing you are pointing at in the first clause. `tap: true` means the step advances when its target is tapped, as well as on Next. This is a tour, not the manual — the manual is the Book and the last step says so.

steps.title: This is the world
steps.body: Seven chains of islands, and the whole war happens on them. Tap a chain to open it.

steps.title: Now open an island
steps.body: Each chain is a handful of islands. Tap this one and you get everything you can do to a place.

steps.title: Everything is on these tabs
steps.body: Who is in the harbor, who is ashore, what is built, and how many troops hold it. This is where you give most of your orders.

steps.title: The little i explains anything
steps.body: Wherever a screen could use a footnote it shows one of these. Tap it and the Book opens at exactly that entry, then hands you straight back.

steps.title: Build is down here
steps.body: Mines and mills that earn, yards that make, fortresses that hold. You pick the thing first and the island second.

steps.title: The Book has everything else
steps.body: Every ship, crew member, troop, building and island in the game, a Rules page that opens with how to win, and a Glossary.

steps.title: The Log is what happened
steps.body: Battles, arrivals, islands changing hands. The number on it is what you have not read, and the panel inside decides what interrupts you.

steps.title: And your advisor is always there
steps.body: Standing on the console, whatever screen you are on. Ask them where to build, who is free, and where the trouble is.

steps.title: Nothing happens until you start the clock
steps.body: Start it and the days turn on their own. Passages take weeks, missions a fortnight ashore, hulls months. Set things going and let it run.

byFaction.empire: Have all three Pirate Lords in irons at the same time. They are people, so you take one by carrying them off a quay — and holding two is worth nothing if the third is still at sea.
byFaction.alliance: Take the young Imperator and Grand Admiral Corvane and hold them at the same time. The Imperator is on Highwater, which is why every war ends up there — but the Grand Admiral is somewhere else.
